questions.question: Practical station: BacT (Powerpoint) isolate - GPC. Catalase positive, PYR negative, DNase negative. Plate looks white, non-hemolytic. Lots of Kirby Bauer discs (novobiocin R).

parts.text: How would you report out susceptibilities?

questions.model_answer:
a) Organism: Staphylococcus saprophyticus (catalase-positive, PYR-negative, DNase-negative, non-hemolytic, and characteristically novobiocin-resistant, distinguishing it from other coagulase-negative staphylococci).
b) Reporting susceptibilities: routine antimicrobial susceptibility testing is generally not indicated/reported for S. saprophyticus from urine, as it is a predictable pathogen of uncomplicated UTI in young women and is reliably susceptible to standard oral agents used for cystitis (e.g., nitrofurantoin, TMP-SMX, beta-lactams) - report the identification with a comment that susceptibility testing is not routinely required rather than a full panel.
questions.beyond_mandell: CLSI guidance on S. saprophyticus susceptibility reporting for uncomplicated UTI.

questions.question: Man with native valve IE, blood grows staph slide coag pos but tube coag neg.

parts.text: Provide the organism ID with its confirmatory test.
What are the susc to pen and ox?

cohort_answer.text: Organism ID: Staph lugdunensis. MALDI (phenotypic: pyr positive). Susc: Resistant to penicillin - blaZ. Sensitive to oxacillin. Penicillin = vast majority of Staphylococci produce a penicillinase blaZ, which confers resistance to penicillin and aminopenicillins. Inhibited readily by β-lactamase inhibitors.

parts.text: A) What microbiological test would differentiate it from S. epidermidis?

cohort_answer.text: Unique resistant to novobiocin, a lab-only antibiotic

questions.question:
Q10 (2016 PM)
When to use cefoxitin disc for isolates of S. aureus and CNST

parts.text: This predicts resistance to which abx?

cohort_answer.text: Oxacillin disk diffusion testing is not reliable for detecting oxacillin resistance and cefoxitin should be used as surrogate instead, because cefoxitin is a better inducer of mecA gene and thus more reliable than oxacillin (detection of BORSA)

parts.text: B) Where does it typically cause infection? What is the risk factor?

cohort_answer.text: Uncomplicated UTI in young sexually active women, second most common cause after E coli. RF: vaginal candidiasis. Complications: acute pyelonephritis, septicemia, nephrolithiasis, endocarditis.
